description: 10 x 20 x 30 mm axis-aligned box, min corner at the origin, modelled as a working engineer does: a 10 x 20 rectangle sketched on XY from the origin, extruded 30 mm along +Z (rebuilt 2026-10-09 from the former {shape: box} primitive request; same body, see the derivation). Locks the sketch + extrude path on the simplest prism, GProp mass properties, exact optimal AABB, B-rep topology counts, and the 0.1 mm linear-deflection tessellation (first golden, 2026-07-10).
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug).
bounding_box = [0,0,0]..[10,20,30]: the sketch rectangle runs (0,0)..(10,20) on XY and the extrude adds +Z 0..30
topology: a rectangular prism is 6 planar faces, 12 straight edges, 1 closed shell
mesh: each planar rectangular face tessellates to exactly 2 triangles (6 * 2 = 12); faceted per-face normals mean no vertex sharing across faces, so 6 faces * 4 corners = 24 vertices

REBUILT AS A FEATURE TREE (2026-10-09): every value above is unchanged from the {shape: box, params: {x: 10, y: 20, z: 30}} primitive this golden used to build. Proof, measured: the two-way boolean difference between the primitive and the sketch + extrude body is empty (0.0 mm^3 both ways), the vertex sets coincide, topology 6/12/1 and mesh 24/12 are identical. GProp now integrates the extruded faces to within 1e-12 of the analytic values (volume 6000.000000000001, area 2199.9999999999995) instead of exactly; the 1e-7 tolerance is unchanged.

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned here: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: CLAUDE.md kernel linear tolerance (1e-7 m convention, applied here in model units). The box is planar-exact in OCCT: GProp integrates planar faces without approximation error, so the measured deviation from analytic was exactly 0.0 for the primitive (verified 2026-07-10, docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md) and is <= 1e-12 for the sketch + extrude tree (2026-10-09). 1e-7 is the standing kernel bound, not a fitted epsilon; loosening it requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
